## These apparel, beauty, and wellness labels don’t just sit around looking good—they are Brands That Matter in 2026


By: Yasmine Gagne |[Link to article](https://www.fastcompany.com/91635516/apparel-wellness-beauty-brands-that-matter-2026-aerie-cerave-crocs-brooklinen-parfums-de-marly-ralph-lauren-my-fitness-pal-essie-bur-bur-reformation-bombas-ralph-lauren-merrell)


With wellness, apparel, and beauty content flooding social media, it can be difficult to stand out. But several brands used unorthodox partnerships and campaigns recently to turn unsexy products like plain bathrobes, Crocs, and dermatologist-approved moisturizer into desirable products. Others, meanwhile, such as Aerie, Bur Bur, and Reformation, found novel ways to double down on their previous bold stances to further promote their authenticity.


**Aerie**
As AI images infiltrate social media ads, presenting viewers with unrealistic body standards and making it hard to distinguish between real and fake, Aerie took a stand. The intimate apparel and lifestyle brand pledged in 2026 not to use the technology in its advertising (it had already pledged not to retouch any images in its campaigns in 2014). To amplify its message, Aerie partnered with Pamela Anderson—who has become famous and revered for her natural look—on a campaign that the brand says generated more than 8.3 billion organic impressions and received 99% positive sentiment.


[Read more](https://www.fastcompany.com/91634509/stacey-mccormick-aerie-brands-that-matter-2026-ai-real-image-pamela-anderson) about Aerie’s Stacey McCormick, one of Fast Company’s CMOs of the Year honorees.
